description: Serving layer in app.py: FastAPI app with permissive CORS, GET / (serve test_page.html), POST /ask, POST /callback, Mangum wrapping for the HTTP path, and the single lambda_handler dispatcher that routes aws:sqs events to the WhatsApp/SQS batch path and everything else to Mangum. Plus the test_page.html test UI. Depends on FEAT-001 (data.py, whatsapp.py) and FEAT-002 (run_agent). Mirrors handler.py's SQS batch shape and reuses whatsapp_lambda extractors via whatsapp.py.
steps: In app.py create app = FastAPI() and add CORSMiddleware with allow_origins=['*'], allow_methods=['*'], allow_headers=['*'] so a file:// HTML page can call the Function URL.
GET / -> return test_page.html contents as HTMLResponse/FileResponse (read the file next to app.py).

POST /ask with a pydantic body {conversation_id: str, message: str}: call agent.run_agent(conversation_id, message); data.append_turn(conversation_id, 'user', message) and data.append_turn(conversation_id, 'assistant', reply); return {'reply': reply, 'conversation_id': conversation_id}.

POST /callback with body {conversation_id: str, receipt_id: str, total_cost}: m = data.get_mapping(conversation_id); compose text = f'Your order is complete. Receipt {receipt_id}. Total cost {total_cost}.'; if WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID env set and m and m.get('whatsapp_number'): whatsapp.send_whatsapp_message(m['whatsapp_number'], text) wrapped in try/except that logs on failure; ALWAYS data.append_turn(conversation_id, 'assistant', text); return {'status': 'ok'}. Never crash when WhatsApp env/number absent.

Add handler = Mangum(app). Implement lambda_handler(event, context): if event.get('Records') and event['Records'][0].get('eventSource') == 'aws:sqs': return process_sqs_batch(event); else return handler(event, context).

Implement process_sqs_batch(event): batch_item_failures=[]; for record in event['Records']: try: webhook = whatsapp.extract_webhook_data(record); for msg in whatsapp.extract_text_messages(webhook): sender=msg['sender']; reply = agent.run_agent(sender, msg['text'], whatsapp_number=sender); data.append_turn(sender,'user',msg['text']); data.append_turn(sender,'assistant',reply); whatsapp.send_whatsapp_message(sender, reply); except Exception: log + append {'itemIdentifier': record.get('messageId')}. Return {'batchItemFailures': batch_item_failures}. (conversation_id == sender so the mapping write in create_order stores the phone number.)

Create test_page.html: vanilla JS + fetch, no build step. Inputs for Function URL base and conversation_id (default a random id), a message box + Send button POSTing {conversation_id, message} to {base}/ask and rendering chat bubbles (including the interrupt/confirm prompt so the user can type 'yes'). A callback section with receipt_id + total_cost inputs and a button POSTing {conversation_id, receipt_id, total_cost} to {base}/callback.
acceptance_criteria: python -c "import app" succeeds and exposes app, handler, lambda_handler.

tests/test_app.py passes (Bedrock/DynamoDB/WhatsApp/run_agent mocked): GET / returns 200 with HTML; POST /ask returns {'reply','conversation_id'} and appends two turns; POST /callback composes the receipt/total message, appends an assistant turn, returns {'status':'ok'}, and does NOT crash when WhatsApp env vars are absent.
lambda_handler routes a synthetic {'Records':[{'eventSource':'aws:sqs',...}]} event to process_sqs_batch (verified by the batchItemFailures-shaped return) and routes a non-SQS event to Mangum.
process_sqs_batch returns {'batchItemFailures': [...]} and isolates per-record failures like handler.py.
verification: python -m pytest tests/test_app.py -q  (offline; TestClient + mocks; all pass)
python -c "import app; assert hasattr(app,'lambda_handler') and hasattr(app,'handler')"
findings:
Implemented and verified offline. Full suite now 23 passed (15 prior FEAT-001/002 + 8 new in tests/test_app.py). Both FEAT-003 verification commands pass: `python -m pytest tests/test_app.py -q` (8 pass) and `python -c "import app; assert hasattr(app,'lambda_handler') and hasattr(app,'handler')"`.

PUBLIC SURFACE (app.py):
- app = FastAPI(title='LangGraph Ordering Agent') with permissive CORSMiddleware (allow_origins/methods/headers = ['*']).
- GET / -> HTMLResponse of test_page.html read from os.path.join(dirname(__file__),'test_page.html').
- POST /ask body AskRequest{conversation_id:str, message:str}: reply = agent.run_agent(conversation_id, message); data.append_turn(user) then data.append_turn(assistant); returns {'reply','conversation_id'}.
- POST /callback body CallbackRequest{conversation_id:str, receipt_id:str, total_cost:object}: text = f'Your order is complete. Receipt {receipt_id}. Total cost {total_cost}.'; sends via whatsapp.send_whatsapp_message ONLY when env WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID set AND data.get_mapping(conversation_id) has 'whatsapp_number' (wrapped in try/except that logs, never raises); ALWAYS data.append_turn(assistant, text); returns {'status':'ok'}. total_cost typed as object so numbers or strings both pass validation (f-string renders either).
- handler = Mangum(app).
- process_sqs_batch(event): per-record try/except; webhook=whatsapp.extract_webhook_data(record); for msg in whatsapp.extract_text_messages(webhook): sender=msg['sender']; reply=agent.run_agent(sender, msg['text'], whatsapp_number=sender); data.append_turn(user)/append_turn(assistant); whatsapp.send_whatsapp_message(sender, reply). On exception logs + appends {'itemIdentifier': messageId} (only when messageId present). Returns {'batchItemFailures':[...]}, mirroring handler.py. conversation_id == sender so create_order's mapping write stores the phone number.
- lambda_handler(event, context): if event is a dict with event['Records'] and Records[0].get('eventSource')=='aws:sqs' -> process_sqs_batch(event); else handler(event, context).

test_page.html: vanilla JS + fetch, no build step. Inputs for Function URL base (trailing slash stripped) and conversation_id (defaults to a random 'conv-xxxx'); chat box POSTing {conversation_id,message} to {base}/ask rendering user/assistant/system bubbles (hint tells the user to type 'yes' to confirm); callback section with receipt_id + total_cost inputs POSTing {conversation_id,receipt_id,total_cost} to {base}/callback.

tests/test_app.py (TestClient; mocks agent.run_agent, data.append_turn/get_mapping, whatsapp.extract_*/send on the app module): GET / returns 200 HTML; POST /ask returns the reply dict and appends two turns; POST /callback composes the receipt/total message + appends an assistant turn + returns {'status':'ok'} with NO WhatsApp env (no send, no crash); /callback sends WhatsApp when configured; /callback does not crash when send raises; lambda_handler routes a synthetic aws:sqs event to process_sqs_batch (patched, asserted) and a non-SQS event to handler/Mangum; process_sqs_batch isolates per-record failures returning {'batchItemFailures':[{'itemIdentifier':'m-bad'}]}.

TEST-INFRA FIX (conftest.py): agent.py builds its LangGraph graph at import time and DynamoDBSaver reads CHECKPOINTER_TABLE_NAME eagerly, so importing agent/app during pytest COLLECTION (before fixtures run) raised KeyError. Added os.environ.setdefault(...) for AWS_REGION + the four table names at conftest module scope so collection-time imports succeed; the autouse _env fixture still re-applies them per test via monkeypatch. This was a pre-existing fragility (tests/test_agent.py alone also failed collection in this env before the fix); production modules were NOT changed.

DEPS: mangum 0.19.0 confirmed installed/importable. Did NOT edit handler.py, whatsapp_lambda.py, agent.py, data.py, checkpointer.py, whatsapp.py, or requirements.txt (requirements reconciliation still deferred per FEAT-001/002 findings). Built against installed langgraph 1.1.3 / fastapi 0.135.2 / mangum 0.19.0.
